body:
Please test this with 4.5.beta4. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104401 might have fixed this issue.

If you are still able to reproduce the issue, please provide an LSP trace from neovim. Also run the following editor script, in the Godot Editor and include its output:

```gdscript
@tool
extends EditorScript

func _run() -> void:
	print(ProjectSettings.globalize_path("res://"))

```

You are basically running Godot on a different machine than Neovim, this use case is not supported. Those project might be the same on disc, but they are available on different paths per machine. So those are in fact different projects path wise.

That's also where the duplicate script name error comes from. Godot sees the script twice. Once from the machine it is running on (`//wsl.localhost/NixOS/home/brady/dev/games/error-test/.../script.gd`). And once through LSP under the path of the linux machine (`/home/brady/dev/games/error-test/.../script.gd`)

Nothing Godot really can do here. Neovim sends paths that are wrong in the context in which Godot is running. You can look whether someone has made some WSL transformer plugin for neovim. I also wrote a [proxy script that transforms LSP paths](https://github.com/HolonProduction/godot-lsp-proxy) a while back, it's totally untested from my side though. Feel free to give it a try.

As for Godot itself, I consider this a wontfix. LSP isn't designed for remote use cases. Hacking some WSL detection on top of a protocol that isn't designed for it will lead to a lot of tech debt.
I found https://github.com/lucasecdb/godot-wsl-lsp which translates the paths and fixes this issue.

You can also filter out certain diagnostics by their message:
```lua
vim.lsp.config("gdscript", {
	handlers = {
		["textDocument/publishDiagnostics"] = function(err, result, ctx)
			local filtered_diagnostics = {}

			for _, diagnostic in ipairs(result.diagnostics) do
				if
					not string.find(diagnostic.message, "hides a global script class") and
					not string.find(diagnostic.message, "Error while getting cache for script") then
					table.insert(filtered_diagnostics, diagnostic)
				end
			end

			result.diagnostics = filtered_diagnostics

			vim.lsp.handlers["textDocument/publishDiagnostics"](err, result, ctx)
		end
	}
})
```
